reviewScope: Every day, all 12 weeks of both pinned plans; production domain event only. No browser or watch claim.

event.consumerScope: Current production APIs consume both frozen old/new generator outputs; baseline has no executionAdjustment API.
event.outcome: Both recommend single-miss without action/confirmation; direct buildExecutionAdjustment returns error, no result, no mutation. Sparse unlogged history remains unknown and does not regenerate.

coverage.300mDisposition: N/A: none in either frozen output. Actual W10 I 400m and W11 RP 400m inspected separately.

findings.expected: A novice with no continuity can keep walk breaks until the longer continuous run feels manageable; instructions explain the transition or offer a readiness choice.
findings.actual: All three W5 runs switch automatically from 5:1 run/walk to continuous Z2 and Monday adds strides; no continuation option appears in generated descriptions.
findings.impact: Potential usability/load mismatch for a novice who has not adapted by W5. This is a product concern, not proof of injury or a failed arithmetic invariant.
findings.recommendation: Explain that walk breaks remain available and base progression on reported execution/readiness.

findings.expected: Distinguish aspirational time, current-fitness pace and unconfirmed endurance without asserting a predicted improvement or guaranteed finish.
findings.actual: Old claims race-day 33:24 and says this low-volume plan is to finish the distance; race card pairs 30:00 with a 35:00 rhythm. New holds current reference at 35:00 and explicitly withholds readiness confirmation.
findings.impact: Old can leave a beginner believing the plan validates finishing or a faster race outcome.

findings.expected: For this very low-base novice, taper retains a small familiar rhythm dose while lowering total load.
findings.actual: Old taper reduces weekly km but its formal work duration rises about 42% relative to W10. New halves RP work to 5.6 minutes and uses more recovery.
findings.impact: Old is less coherent as a novice taper. RP is slower than I, so more minutes alone is not proof that total intensity load rose.
findings.recommendation: Retain new reduced-dose taper; assess duration and intensity together.

evidence.focus: DELOAD — obim dole, ostaje kratka oštrina

findings.expected: Week focus describes the delivered novice sessions.
findings.actual: Focus promises retained short sharpness even though W4 contains only run/walk and optional strength.
findings.impact: Small expectation mismatch; day instructions are otherwise coherent.
findings.recommendation: Use base/run-walk deload focus when no strides or session is delivered.

evidence.text: Deonice skraćene radi poštovanja budžeta rada.

findings.expected: Explain the user purpose: short controlled repetitions as an introduction, with clear recovery instructions.
findings.actual: Notes expose the internal work-budget mechanism without explaining what the short dose is intended to train.
findings.impact: Minor comprehension issue; the prescription, current-fitness zone and arithmetic remain coherent.
findings.recommendation: Replace internal budgeting language with a plain purpose and effort cue.
